AT0001.title: Black SIM Cards
AT0001.description: Black SIM cards, also known as 'black phone cards', refer to mobile phone cards (including wireless data cards) that have not been registered under a real name and are used by criminals for illegal activities. Since the implementation of phone real-name registration in September 2013, new users in China have largely completed real-name registration. However, due to lax enforcement and large existing stock, unregistered phone cards still number as many as 180 million, giving criminals opportunities to spread obscene content, commit telecommunications fraud, and organize terrorist activities. The main sources of black SIM cards are physical carrier cards, virtual carrier cards, and overseas phone cards.

references.title: Notice on Lawfully Cleaning Up Fraud-Related Phone Cards, IoT Cards, and Associated Internet Accounts
Telephone User Real Identity Information Registration Regulations

AT0001-002.title: Modem Pool SIM Cards
AT0001-002.description: Black SIM cards used with a 'modem pool' — a network communication hardware device that enables simultaneous multi-number calling and bulk SMS sending. A modem pool can hold dozens of SIM cards operating in parallel and is widely used by black-market actors for GOIP voice relay, bulk scam SMS, and batch OTP reception, serving as the core communications infrastructure for telecom fraud and OTP-receiving platforms.

references.title: Jiangsu Mobile Cracks Down on Modem Pools, Providing 6,363 GOIP Clues to Police

AT0001-003.title: Intercept SIM Cards
AT0001-003.description: SIM cards that, via malware or trojans, grant unauthorized control over a real user's SMS and verification code reception, typically sourced from intercept card platforms. Attackers use trojans implanted on the victim's phone to capture OTPs in real time and then impersonate the victim to register accounts, log in, and move funds, making this a key tool for bypassing SMS two-factor authentication and conducting account takeover and card fraud.

references.title: Black Market Big Data: 2025 Annual Summary of Internet Black-Grey Market Trends
